technical-writing: In the Diataxis documentation framework, which type of page is meant to teach a beginner by walking them through a complete small project?
Tutorial
Reference
Explanation
How-to guide
Diataxis separates learning-oriented tutorials from task-oriented how-to guides, information-oriented reference and understanding-oriented explanation.
A reader already knows the product and wants to rotate an API key. Which Diataxis document type best serves this need?
How-to guide
Tutorial
Explanation
Release note
How-to guides are goal-oriented steps for a user who already has basic competence. A tutorial is for learning from scratch.
Which heading structure is best for a documentation page that will be scanned quickly?
Descriptive, task-based headings in a consistent hierarchy (H1, then H2, then H3)
Clever, playful headings that hide the topic until the reader opens them
One long H1 heading followed by unbroken paragraphs of prose
Headings that skip levels freely (H1, then H4, then H2) so the page looks more varied
Readers scan headings to find what they need, so headings should state the topic plainly and follow a logical hierarchy.
Which sentence follows common technical writing guidance best?
Run the installer, then restart the server.
The installer should be run, after which a restart of the server is to be performed.
It is recommended that the installer be run and the server restarted.
A restart of the server is needed once installation has been done by you.
Clear technical writing prefers active voice, imperative mood for instructions and short sentences.
What should an API reference entry for an endpoint include at minimum?
Method and path, typed parameters, request and response examples, error codes
A history of why the endpoint was designed and which engineer wrote it
Only a short summary of the endpoint, since developers can always read the source code
A marketing description of the business benefits the endpoint brings
Reference docs are for lookup, so they must be complete and precise about inputs, outputs and failures.
An API parameter is documented as "limit: the limit". What is the main problem?
It repeats the name without saying type, allowed range or default
It should be rewritten in passive voice, as reference style guides usually require
Parameter names must never appear in their own description
It is too long for a reference table
A useful parameter description states what it controls, its type, valid values and default, not just the name again.
Which code sample is most helpful in an API reference?
A minimal, runnable example with realistic values and the expected response
A large excerpt of real production code, including the unrelated business logic around it
Pseudocode that hides the real request format
A screenshot of code that cannot be copied
Copyable, minimal and realistic samples let developers verify behavior quickly. Screenshots and pseudocode block copying and testing.
You are writing a developer guide. Where should prerequisites (accounts, versions, tools) appear?
At the start, before the first step
At the very end, after the troubleshooting section
Inside a footnote attached to the last step
Only in the separate API reference pages
Listing prerequisites first prevents readers from failing midway because something is missing.
In a step-by-step guide, why should each numbered step usually contain a single action?
Readers can follow and verify progress one action at a time
Markdown limits each numbered list item to a single sentence of text
Search engines rank one-action steps higher
It makes the guide longer, which looks more thorough
One action per step reduces missed actions and makes it easy to tell where something went wrong.
Which section is most important to put near the top of a project README?
What the project does and how to install and run it quickly
The full list of contributors, their roles and how to contact each of them
The complete changelog since the first commit
Detailed internal architecture of every module
A README is the entry point, so it should first answer what this is and how to get started.
A README says "Run npm start" but the project needs environment variables first. What is the best fix?
Add a setup step listing the required variables, such as a .env.example file
Remove the npm start instruction so that nobody runs into the error
Mention the variables only in a comment on the issue tracker, where maintainers will see it
Tell users to search the source code to discover the variables
Quick-start instructions must work as written. Documenting required configuration, often via a .env.example, makes the first run succeed.
What is the main purpose of a documentation style guide?
Keeping terminology, tone and formatting consistent across many authors
Replacing the need for engineers to technically review documentation content
Defining the product roadmap for the documentation team
Setting the visual brand colors of the marketing site
Style guides like the Google developer documentation style guide or the Microsoft Writing Style Guide keep docs consistent regardless of who writes them.
A style guide says to use one term consistently. A page alternates between "workspace", "project" and "space" for the same thing. Why is this a problem?
Readers may assume they are three different concepts
Search engines penalize pages that use synonyms for the same feature
It makes the page shorter than it should be
Only the first term will be translated correctly
Technical readers treat different words as different things. Using one term per concept prevents confusion.
Which guideline appears in widely used developer style guides such as Google's and Microsoft's?
Address the reader as "you" and use second person
Refer to the reader as "the user" in third person throughout
Use first person plural "we" for every instruction
Avoid pronouns and write only in passive voice
Both major developer style guides recommend second person, which makes instructions direct and clear.
What is the main audience and purpose of release notes?
Telling users what changed in a version and how it affects them
Recording every internal commit message verbatim for the team
Explaining the long-term product vision to investors
Teaching brand new users the basics of the product step by step
Release notes summarize user-visible changes, fixes and required actions for a specific version.
Which release note entry is best written?
Fixed: exporting a report with over 10,000 rows no longer times out.
Fixed bug #4821 reported by the QA team last sprint.
Refactored the ExportService class and tweaked several internal timeout values.
Various performance improvements and fixes under the hood.
A good entry describes the user-visible effect. Ticket numbers or internal class names alone do not tell users what changed.
A new version removes a deprecated API parameter. How should the release notes handle this?
Flag it clearly as a breaking change and describe the migration path
Leave it out entirely so that users are not alarmed by the change
Mention it only in a code comment inside the SDK source
List it at the bottom of the notes under minor improvements
Breaking changes need prominent placement and migration instructions so users can upgrade safely.
Under Semantic Versioning (SemVer 2.0.0), which version bump signals a backward-incompatible API change?
Major, for example 2.4.1 to 3.0.0
Minor, for example 2.4.1 to 2.5.0
Patch, for example 2.4.1 to 2.4.2
Pre-release, for example 2.4.1 to 2.4.1-beta
SemVer reserves the major number for incompatible API changes, minor for backward-compatible features and patch for backward-compatible fixes.
What does the Keep a Changelog convention recommend as section headings within a version entry?
Added, Changed, Deprecated, Removed, Fixed, Security
Features, Chores, Refactors, Tests, Docs, Builds, Style
Major, Minor, Patch, Build, Alpha, Beta
Frontend, Backend, Database, DevOps, QA, Design
Keep a Changelog groups changes by type of impact on users, using exactly these six categories.
Which technique best checks whether a tutorial actually works for new readers?
Have a newcomer follow it exactly and note where they get stuck
Ask the original author to reread it once more before publishing
Run a spell checker and a grammar checker over the whole text
Count the words to make sure it is long enough to be thorough
Authors fill gaps from memory. Watching a newcomer follow the steps reveals missing steps and unclear wording.
public-speaking: Which slide design choice usually makes a technical talk easier to follow?
One main idea per slide with a short headline that states it
Fitting the full script onto each slide so nothing is forgotten
Using a new font and color theme on every slide for variety
Putting all charts on one slide so the audience sees everything
One idea per slide with an assertive headline lets the audience grasp the point while listening to you.
A speaker reads dense bullet points word for word from the slides. What is the most likely effect?
The audience reads ahead and stops listening to the speaker
The audience remembers far more of the content than with spoken delivery
The talk feels more interactive and personal
Questions become shorter and more focused
People cannot read and listen at the same time well, so dense text competes with the speaker instead of supporting them.
What is a strong way to open a 10 minute project presentation?
Open with the problem or a concrete hook, then say what they will gain
Apologize for being nervous and for any mistakes you might make
Spend the first three minutes listing your team's biographies and previous projects
Begin with the detailed table of database fields and their types
A hook plus a clear promise gives the audience a reason to listen. Apologies reduce credibility.
Which structure is commonly recommended for a short persuasive talk?
Problem, solution, evidence, call to action
Thanks, agenda, appendix, references
Details, background, conclusion, introduction
Questions first, then the main content, then the agenda
Problem, solution, evidence and a clear ask is a simple persuasive arc audiences can follow.
During a talk you notice many people looking at their phones. What is the best adjustment?
Re-engage them with a question, a quick poll or a concrete example
Speak noticeably faster so you finish before they lose interest completely
Stop and tell the audience to put their phones away
Skip to the appendix slides with detailed tables
Interaction or a vivid example resets attention. Speeding up or scolding usually makes things worse.
Why do speakers often tell a short personal or user story in a technical talk?
Stories make abstract information concrete and easier to remember
Stories replace the need for any data or evidence
Stories make the talk longer, which makes the speaker look more serious and prepared
Audiences expect stories only at the very end
A story gives context and emotion, which helps audiences remember the point. It should support evidence, not replace it.
In storytelling, what is the role of conflict or tension?
It creates a problem the audience wants to see resolved
It shows the audience that the speaker disagrees with their opinions
It replaces the conclusion of the talk
It is used only in fiction, not in business talks
Tension, such as a failing system or an unmet need, makes the audience care about the resolution you present.
Which is the best way to use a pause while speaking?
Pause briefly after a key point to let it land
Avoid pauses entirely to show confidence
Fill every pause with "um" so the audience knows you are thinking
Pause only when you lose your place in the notes
A deliberate pause signals importance and gives listeners time to process. Filler words weaken delivery.
A speaker is told they talk too fast when nervous. Which practice helps most?
Rehearse aloud with a timer and mark planned pauses in the notes
Add more slides so there is more to say
Memorize the full script word for word and recite it as quickly as possible
Drink an energy drink just before going on stage
Timed rehearsal and planned pauses build a natural pace. Cramming more content increases speed.
What does "vocal variety" mean in public speaking?
Changing pitch, pace and volume to emphasize meaning
Switching between several languages during one talk
Using a microphone and a backup microphone
Repeating each sentence twice for clarity
Varying pitch, pace and volume keeps attention and highlights what matters. A monotone voice loses listeners.
An audience member asks a question you cannot answer. What is the best response?
Say you do not know, and offer to follow up after checking
Invent a plausible answer on the spot to avoid looking unprepared
Ignore the question and move to the next slide
Tell them the question is not relevant
Honesty preserves credibility. Following up shows respect for the question.
Why should a speaker repeat or paraphrase a question from the audience before answering?
So the whole room hears it and you confirm you understood it
To buy extra time so that the session can run over schedule
Because conference rules require every question to be repeated
To show the audience that the question was too simple to ask
Repeating the question ensures the whole room hears it and lets you check you understood it correctly.
An audience member makes a long statement with no clear question during Q&A. What is the most professional response?
Briefly summarize their point, respond, and invite the next question
Let them continue for as long as they want, then end the session
Interrupt sharply and tell them this is not a question at all
End the whole Q&A session immediately and leave the stage
A brief summary and response respects the person while protecting time for other questions.
You present to non-technical managers about a system migration. What should you focus on?
Business impact, risks, timeline and the decision you need from them
Code snippets, full database schemas and the deployment scripts
The exact versions of every library and framework that the new system depends on
A deep dive into the math behind the migration algorithm
Tailor the talk to the audience: managers need impact and decisions, not implementation details.
What is the main benefit of a live demo in a technical presentation, and the main risk?
It proves the product works, but can fail, so keep a recorded backup
It is faster than slides, but audiences usually find demos boring
It needs no rehearsal, but it always requires internet access
It replaces Q&A, but it also makes any slides unnecessary
Demos are convincing but fragile. Rehearsal and a pre-recorded fallback are standard practice.
You must show code in a talk. Which approach is best?
Show a short snippet in a large font and highlight the lines that matter
Show the whole source file in a small font so that nothing important is missing
Show code only as a link and never on the slide
Scroll quickly through the code in your editor
Large, short and highlighted code lets the room read the relevant part. Full files in small fonts are unreadable.
When presenting a chart in a talk, what should you do first?
Explain what the axes show, then state the key takeaway
Read every number in the chart aloud
Move on immediately and let the audience interpret it
Apologize for the chart's colors
Orient the audience to the axes, then tell them what to see, so everyone draws the right conclusion.
Which ending is strongest for a talk?
Restate the key message and give a clear next step or call to action
Say "that's all I have" and simply stop speaking at that point
Introduce a brand new topic so the audience leaves feeling curious
Show a slide with only the word "Questions?" and wait silently
A strong close restates the main idea and tells the audience what to do or remember.
What is the most effective way to reduce stage anxiety before a talk?
Rehearse several times aloud, ideally in front of others
Avoid rehearsing so the talk feels spontaneous
Read the slides silently once the night before, so the talk stays fresh
Write the talk on the day it is given
Repeated out-loud rehearsal builds familiarity and confidence, and reveals timing problems.
Where should a speaker usually look while talking to a live audience?
At different people across the room, a few seconds each
At the projected slides behind them for most of the time
At their own printed notes for nearly the whole talk
At one fixed point on the back wall above everyone's heads
Eye contact with individuals across the room builds connection. Facing the slides turns your back to the audience.
product-management: Which is the standard user story template?
As a <type of user>, I want <goal> so that <benefit>
The system shall <function> within <time limit> for <role>
Given <context>, when <event>, then <outcome>
If <condition> then <action> else <fallback>
The role, goal and benefit template keeps the focus on who needs something and why. Given/When/Then is a format for acceptance criteria.
What are acceptance criteria for a user story?
Conditions a story must meet for the product owner to accept it
A list of the developers who are assigned to work on the story
The estimated hours that each task in the story will take
The design mockups and screenshots attached to the story ticket
Acceptance criteria define the testable conditions of satisfaction for a specific story.
Which acceptance criterion is best written?
Given a logged-in user, when they click Export, then a CSV downloads
The export feature should work well and be fast for every user, on every device
Export must be user-friendly, intuitive and pleasant to use
Developers should implement exporting properly and test it
Good criteria are specific and testable. Given/When/Then makes the precondition, action and expected result explicit.
What does the INVEST acronym describe?
Qualities of a good user story: Independent, Negotiable, Valuable, Estimable, Small, Testable
Steps of a product launch: Inform, Notify, Validate, Execute, Ship, Track, Review
Metrics for investors: Income, Net value, Volume, Equity, Sales, Turnover
Roles in a Scrum team: Investor, Negotiator, Visionary, Engineer, Sponsor, Tester
INVEST, coined by Bill Wake, is a checklist for writing user stories that are ready for development.
What is the main difference between a product roadmap and a release plan?
A roadmap shows direction and themes over time; a release plan details what ships when
A roadmap lists the bugs the team must fix; a release plan lists the company's annual budget
A roadmap is only for engineers; a release plan is only for the sales team
A roadmap is fixed for several years; a release plan can never be changed
Roadmaps communicate outcomes and priorities at a high level; release plans are tactical and date-specific.
A Now / Next / Later roadmap is often preferred over a date-based roadmap because:
It shows priorities without committing to dates that may change
It removes the need for the team to prioritize any of the work
It lists every task in the backlog along with hour estimates
It is the roadmap format that the Scrum Guide requires teams to use
Now/Next/Later shows sequence and focus while staying honest about uncertainty in later items.
What is the main goal of backlog refinement (backlog grooming)?
Clarifying, splitting, estimating and ordering upcoming backlog items
Reviewing the completed increment with stakeholders and collecting their feedback
Reflecting on how the team worked during the last sprint
Deploying finished features to production
Refinement keeps the top of the backlog ready for upcoming sprints. Reviewing the increment happens in the Sprint Review.
According to the Scrum Guide, who is accountable for ordering the Product Backlog?
The Product Owner
The Scrum Master
The Developers
The most senior stakeholder
The Scrum Guide makes the Product Owner accountable for Product Backlog management, including ordering items.
A backlog has grown to 600 items, many years old. What is a sensible refinement action?
Archive or delete stale items that no longer align with goals
Estimate every single item in detail with the whole team before the next sprint
Move all items into the current sprint
Split each item into ten smaller tasks
A huge, stale backlog hides priorities. Removing items that no longer matter keeps it useful.
What is a Minimum Viable Product (MVP)?
The smallest version that lets a team learn whether customers value it
A complete product with every planned feature, released to customers as a beta
The cheapest product version the company can sell to customers
A clickable design prototype that cannot be used for real tasks
Popularized by Eric Ries, an MVP is about validated learning with the least effort, not about shipping a cheap or full product.
A team wants to test demand for a meal-planning app before building it. Which is a valid MVP-style experiment?
A landing page describing the app with a sign-up button
Building the full app with all integrations before any launch
Hiring a large sales team before any product exists at all
Writing a 50 page specification and waiting for approval
A landing page (smoke test) measures real interest cheaply before investing in development.
What is the main purpose of tracking a North Star Metric?
Focusing the team on one metric that reflects core customer value
Replacing all of the other metrics that the company tracks
Measuring the individual performance of each employee on the team
Reporting the company's stock price to every team each day
A North Star Metric aligns teams around the value customers get. Supporting metrics are still tracked.
Which of these is a vanity metric rather than an actionable metric?
Total registered users since launch
Week-1 retention rate of new sign-ups
Conversion rate from trial to paid
Weekly active users divided by monthly active users
A cumulative total only goes up and says little about health. Rates and ratios guide decisions.
Monthly churn rate is calculated as:
Customers lost during the month divided by customers at the start of the month
New customers during the month divided by total customers
Revenue during the month divided by number of customers
Customers at the end of the month divided by customers at the start of the month
Churn measures the share of existing customers who leave over a period.
What does DAU/MAU measure?
Stickiness: how often monthly users return on a typical day
Average revenue earned per monthly active user in each calendar month
The number of new app downloads recorded per day
The ratio of paid subscribers to free users each month
Dividing daily by monthly active users shows how habitually people use the product.
In the RICE prioritization framework, how is the score calculated?
(Reach x Impact x Confidence) / Effort
Reach + Impact + Confidence + Effort
(Reach x Effort) / (Impact x Confidence)
Reach x Impact x Confidence x Effort
RICE, from Intercom, rewards reach, impact and confidence and divides by effort, so cheap high-value items rank first.
Feature A: Reach 1000, Impact 2, Confidence 50%, Effort 2. Feature B: Reach 500, Impact 3, Confidence 100%, Effort 1. Which has the higher RICE score?
Feature B, with a score of 1500
Feature A, with a score of 1000
Feature A, with a score of 2000
Neither, they tie at 500 each
A: 1000 x 2 x 0.5 / 2 = 500. B: 500 x 3 x 1.0 / 1 = 1500, so B ranks higher despite smaller reach.
In the MoSCoW method, what does the "W" stand for?
Won't have (this time)
Wish list
Will have later this sprint
Weighted priority
MoSCoW is Must have, Should have, Could have, Won't have this time. The last category sets explicit scope limits.
Under MoSCoW, a feature without which the release would be unusable or illegal is a:
Must have
Should have
Could have
Won't have
Must haves are non-negotiable for the release. Should haves are important but the release still works without them.
In the Kano model, what are "delighters" (attractive features)?
Unexpected features that raise satisfaction but are not missed when absent
Basic features whose absence makes customers very dissatisfied
Features whose satisfaction rises in proportion to how much is delivered
Features that customers actively dislike when they are added
Kano separates must-be, performance and attractive qualities. Delighters surprise users without being expected.
ui-ux-design: What is the main purpose of a low-fidelity wireframe?
Exploring layout and structure quickly before visual polish
Delivering final pixel-perfect assets to developers for build
Testing the final color palette and brand fonts with users
Producing marketing images for the app store listing
Low-fidelity wireframes are cheap to change, so teams can test structure and flow early.
Why do designers often use grayscale and placeholder text in early wireframes?
To keep feedback on structure and flow instead of colors and copy
Because most wireframing tools do not support color at all
Because developers require grayscale files when they implement the first version
To make the wireframe load faster when shared in the browser
Without visual polish, reviewers comment on layout and content priority, which is what matters at that stage.
What is a user persona?
A fictional but research-based profile representing a key user group
A real customer who is chosen by the team to approve every design decision
A list of all user accounts in the database
The designer's own preferences written as a profile
Personas summarize patterns from real research so the team can design for specific needs and goals.
Which research method best reveals why users abandon a checkout flow?
Moderated usability sessions where users think aloud at checkout
A survey asking users to rate the brand on a scale from 1 to 10
Counting page views on the homepage over the last month
Asking the sales team what they think customers dislike
Observing users think aloud uncovers the reasons behind behavior. Analytics show where they leave but not why.
What is the difference between qualitative and quantitative user research?
Qualitative explains why people behave as they do; quantitative measures how many
Qualitative relies on numbers; quantitative relies on open interviews
Qualitative is done after launch; quantitative is done only before launch
Qualitative is optional for teams; quantitative is mandatory for every project
Interviews and usability tests answer why; surveys and analytics answer how many.
According to Nielsen Norman Group, roughly how many users are typically enough for a small qualitative usability test to find most common problems?
About 5
About 50
About 500
Exactly 1
NN/g research shows around 5 users uncover most usability problems in a qualitative test; iterating with more small rounds is more efficient.
During a usability test, a participant asks "Should I click here?" What should the facilitator do?
Reply neutrally, for example "What would you expect to happen?"
Say yes and point to the correct button so the test continues
Explain in detail how the feature was designed to work
End the session early, since the user is clearly confused
Facilitators avoid leading participants so the test shows how real users behave without help.
What is the difference between a usability test and A/B testing?
Usability tests find problems with a few users; A/B tests compare variants at scale
Usability tests need thousands of users; A/B tests need only about five users per variant
They are the same research method, just known by different names
A/B tests explain why users struggle; usability tests only count clicks
Usability testing is qualitative and diagnostic; A/B testing is quantitative and measures which variant performs better.
A date field accepts free text and rejects bad formats only after the form is submitted. Which Nielsen heuristic suggests a date picker or inline validation?
Error prevention
Aesthetic and minimalist design
Consistency and standards
Help and documentation
Error prevention means designing so mistakes are less likely in the first place, for example by constraining input with a date picker.
A loading button shows no spinner or change after it is clicked. Which Nielsen heuristic is violated?
Visibility of system status
Consistency and standards
Flexibility and efficiency of use
Match between system and real world
Users should always know what the system is doing through timely feedback.
Showing recently used files in a menu instead of asking users to type a filename supports which heuristic?
Recognition rather than recall
User control and freedom
Error prevention
Aesthetic and minimalist design
Making options visible reduces memory load: recognizing is easier than recalling.
Which heuristic is supported by providing Undo and a clear Cancel button?
User control and freedom
Visibility of system status
Help and documentation
Recognition rather than recall
Users make mistakes and need a clearly marked emergency exit to leave unwanted states.
What is card sorting used for?
Learning how users group and label content for navigation
Testing how fast pages load on different mobile devices
Choosing the brand color palette with input from users
Ranking reported bugs by severity before a release
In card sorting, participants organize topics into groups, revealing their mental models for navigation.
What does tree testing evaluate?
Whether users can find items in a text-only navigation hierarchy
How fast the site's database queries run under heavy load
Which illustration style users prefer for the landing page hero section
How the page layout adapts to different screen sizes
Tree testing checks the findability of a text-only hierarchy, isolating information architecture from visual design.
What is the main benefit of a design system?
Reusable components and shared rules that keep products consistent
A single static mockup of the homepage shared with the team
A complete replacement for user research and usability testing
A brand logo file exported in several formats and sizes
Design systems combine components, tokens and documentation so teams build consistent interfaces faster.
In Atomic Design (Brad Frost), what is the correct order from smallest to largest?
Atoms, molecules, organisms, templates, pages
Pages, templates, organisms, molecules, atoms
Molecules, atoms, templates, organisms, pages
Atoms, organisms, molecules, pages, templates
Atomic Design builds up from atoms (a button) to molecules (a search field) to organisms (a header), then templates and pages.
Which technique most directly creates visual hierarchy on a page?
Varying size, weight, contrast and spacing of elements
Using the same font size and weight for every element
Centering every element on the page along one axis
Adding more items to the main navigation bar
Hierarchy comes from contrast: bigger, bolder, higher-contrast and well-spaced elements are seen first.
Per WCAG 2.x level AA, what is the minimum contrast ratio for normal-size body text?
WCAG AA requires 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text. 7:1 is the AAA level.
What does Fitts's law imply for interface design?
Larger and closer targets are faster to click or tap
Users read every page in a strict left-to-right, top-to-bottom order
More choices always make decisions faster
Users remember about seven items at once
Fitts's law relates target size and distance to movement time, so key actions should be large and easy to reach.
What does Hick's law state?
Decision time grows with the number and complexity of choices
Users tend to click the first option they see on any page
Larger buttons get clicked more often regardless of position
Users stop reading most pages after about three paragraphs
Hick's law suggests reducing or grouping choices to speed up decisions.
figma: In Figma, what keyboard shortcut adds Auto Layout to a selected frame or set of layers?
Shift + A
Ctrl/Cmd + G
Ctrl/Cmd + Alt/Option + K
Shift + R
Shift + A adds Auto Layout. Ctrl/Cmd + G groups layers, Ctrl/Cmd + Alt/Option + K creates a component.
A button uses Auto Layout. You want it to grow wider as the label text gets longer. Which horizontal resizing setting should the button frame use?
Hug contents
Fixed width
Fill container
Scale
Hug contents makes the frame size itself to its children, so longer text widens the button.
Inside an Auto Layout row, you want one child to take all remaining horizontal space. Which setting does that child need?
Fill container
Hug contents
Fixed width
Absolute position
Fill container makes a child stretch to fill the available space along that axis.
In Auto Layout, what does "space between" spacing mode do?
Pushes children to the edges and spreads leftover space evenly between them
Adds a fixed 8 px gap between every child, regardless of how wide the frame becomes
Stacks all children on top of each other in the same position
Places all children at the start of the frame with no gap at all
Space between (similar to CSS justify-content: space-between) spreads children across the full frame.
How do you make one layer inside an Auto Layout frame ignore the layout flow, such as a badge pinned to a corner?
Enable Absolute position on that layer
Lock the layer
Set its opacity to 0 and duplicate it
Convert the parent frame to a group
Absolute position lets a child be placed freely while siblings keep their Auto Layout flow.
What is the relationship between a main component and its instances in Figma?
Main component changes reach instances, except properties overridden there
Instances are fully independent copies with no link to the main component
Changes made to any instance automatically update the main component
Instances can only be used in the same file as their main component
Instances inherit from the main component; local overrides such as changed text are preserved.
You have Primary, Secondary and Ghost buttons in Small and Large sizes. What is the best way to organize them in Figma?
One component set with variant properties Type and Size
Six separate components with unrelated names on one page
One component with all six buttons drawn inside one frame
Six groups copied by hand into each design file that needs them
Variants combine related components into a set with properties, making swapping easy in the instance panel.
Which Figma component property lets designers show or hide an icon in instances without creating extra variants?
Boolean property
Instance swap property
Text property
Variant property
A boolean property toggles a layer's visibility, avoiding a separate variant for each with/without combination.
Which component property lets an instance replace its nested icon with any other icon component?
Instance swap property
Boolean property
Text property
Constraint property
Instance swap properties expose a nested instance so users can pick a different component in place.
What does the "Detach instance" action do?
Turns it into a regular frame that no longer gets main component updates
Deletes the main component from the published team library and from every file
Moves the instance to a new page and hides the original
Publishes the instance as a brand new shared team library
Detaching breaks the link to the main component, so future changes no longer apply.
In Figma, what are variables most commonly used to implement?
Design tokens such as colors and spacing, with modes like light and dark
Animated transitions between frames in an interactive prototype
Plugins written in JavaScript that automate repetitive tasks across many files
Version history snapshots that let you restore older file states
Variables store reusable values and support modes, which makes them the native way to represent design tokens.
A team wants one set of color values for light theme and another for dark theme, switchable on a frame. Which Figma feature fits?
A variable collection with Light and Dark modes
Two separate copies of every frame in the file
A shared layout grid style applied to each frame
A new branch of the file for each color theme
Variable modes let the same variable resolve to different values; you set the mode on a frame or page.
Why do design systems often use alias (semantic) tokens such as color/text/primary that point to raw tokens such as blue/600?
So meaning stays stable while the raw value can change in one place
Because Figma does not allow raw color values on any layer
To make each token name longer and therefore more unique across the whole file
Because alias tokens render faster in interactive prototypes
Semantic tokens describe purpose; changing the referenced primitive updates every usage consistently.
In a Figma prototype, what does the Smart Animate transition do?
Animates matching layers between two frames, based on layer names
Generates new intermediate frames automatically using AI
Plays a video file that is embedded inside the frame
Converts the prototype into production-ready CSS animations for developers
Smart Animate finds layers with the same name in both frames and animates differences in position, size, opacity and more.
Smart Animate between two frames shows a sudden jump instead of a smooth move for a card. What is the most likely cause?
The card layer has different names in the two frames
The prototype connection uses the On click trigger
Both frames are placed on the same page of the file
The card has a drop shadow effect applied to it
Smart Animate matches layers by name (and hierarchy). Different names mean it treats them as different layers and cuts.
Which prototype feature in Figma keeps a header visible while the rest of a long frame scrolls?
Set the header's scroll behavior to Fixed
Set the header layer's opacity to 100%
Add a column layout grid to the header
Bind the header's height to a variable
Scroll behavior settings on a layer, such as Fixed, keep it in place while content scrolls in the prototype.
What is the main benefit of using shared color and text styles instead of raw values?
Updating a style changes every layer that uses it
Styles make the file size smaller in all cases
Styles are required to export images
Styles automatically pass accessibility checks
Styles centralize visual values, so a single edit updates everywhere they are applied.
How do you make your file's styles and components available in other team files?
Publish them as a team library
Export the file as PNG
Copy the file link into a comment
Duplicate the file for each team member
Publishing to a library lets other files enable it and use, then update, its styles and components.
A 12-column layout grid is set with Stretch type. What happens to the column widths when the frame is resized?
Columns resize to fill the frame; margins and gutters stay fixed
Columns keep a fixed width and the outer margins grow instead
The number of columns changes automatically to fit the frame
The grid disappears until the frame is reset to its original size
Stretch grids have flexible column widths with fixed gutters and margins, similar to responsive CSS grids.
What do constraints control for a layer inside a regular (non-Auto Layout) frame?
How the layer moves or resizes when the parent frame is resized
The order in which layers appear in the layers panel when the frame is resized
The export format of the layer
Which users can edit the layer
Constraints like Left, Right, Center or Scale define how a child responds when its frame changes size.
data-analysis: What is the main goal of Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA)?
Understanding the data's structure, quirks and relationships before modeling
Deploying a trained model to production and monitoring its predictions for real users
Writing the final polished report for executives
Proving a hypothesis that was chosen in advance
EDA, promoted by John Tukey, uses summaries and plots to learn what the data looks like and what questions are worth asking.
A column of incomes has mean 95,000 and median 52,000. What does this most likely indicate?
The distribution is right-skewed by a few very high incomes
The distribution is perfectly symmetric
The distribution is left-skewed by a few very low incomes
The data contains no outliers
When the mean is far above the median, a long right tail of large values is pulling the mean up.
Which plot is best for quickly checking the distribution shape of one numeric variable?
Histogram
Pie chart
Line chart over categories
Stacked bar chart
A histogram shows how values are distributed across bins, revealing skew, modes and gaps.
Using the IQR rule, a value is commonly flagged as an outlier when it is:
Below Q1 - 1.5 x IQR or above Q3 + 1.5 x IQR
More than 1.5 times the mean
Below the median or above the mean by more than one unit
Outside the range of Q1 to Q3
The 1.5 x IQR fence is Tukey's standard rule and is what box plot whiskers usually use.
What does a Pearson correlation coefficient of r = -0.9 between two variables indicate?
A strong negative linear relationship
A weak negative relationship
No relationship at all
That one variable causes the other to fall
r near -1 means that as one variable rises, the other tends to fall along a line. Correlation alone does not show causation.
Pearson r between X and Y is close to 0, but a scatter plot shows a clear U-shape. What is the correct conclusion?
There is a strong non-linear relationship that r misses
X and Y are completely unrelated to each other
The scatter plot must have been drawn incorrectly
The data must contain a calculation error somewhere
Pearson r measures only linear association. Always plot the data, as Anscombe's quartet famously shows.
Ice cream sales and drowning incidents are positively correlated. What is the most likely explanation?
A confounding variable, hot weather, drives both
Eating ice cream causes drowning
Drowning causes people to buy ice cream
The strong correlation proves a direct causal link between them
Both rise in summer. A third variable creating a spurious correlation is a classic confounder example.
Which correlation measure is more appropriate for ranked data or a monotonic but non-linear relationship?
Spearman rank correlation
Pearson correlation
Covariance in raw units
Coefficient of variation
Spearman correlation works on ranks, so it captures any monotonic relationship and is robust to outliers.
A dataset has a Country column with values "USA", "usa", "U.S.A." and "United States". What is the right cleaning step?
Standardize them to one canonical value before grouping
Delete every row whose country is not "USA"
Leave them as they are, since grouping will merge them
Convert the column to numeric type
Inconsistent labels split one category into several groups, so they must be normalized first.
Values in an age column are missing for 3% of rows, at random. Which is a reasonable simple approach for a quick analysis?
Impute with the median or drop those rows, and document it
Replace every missing age with 0 so no rows are lost
Fill each missing age with the maximum age in the column
Delete the whole age column from the dataset entirely
Replacing with 0 creates impossible values. Median imputation or dropping a small random share is reasonable if documented.
After joining orders to customers, the row count is larger than the original orders table. What is the most likely cause?
Duplicate keys in the customers table multiplied the rows
The join removed all orders that had no matching customer
The orders table was sorted in the wrong order before joining
The join converted every date column into plain text values
If a customer ID appears twice in the customer table, each matching order is duplicated. Check key uniqueness before joining.
What is the purpose of a moving average (for example, a 7-day rolling mean) in trend analysis?
Smoothing short-term noise so the underlying trend is visible
Removing all outliers from the data permanently before analysis
Forecasting exact future values for each of the coming days
Converting the raw values into percentages of the total
Rolling averages reduce day-to-day fluctuations, such as weekday effects, revealing the longer trend.
Retail sales jump every December and drop in January. What kind of pattern is this?
Seasonality
A random walk
A long-term trend reversal
Measurement error
A pattern that repeats at a fixed calendar interval is seasonality, which should be separated from the trend.
Why compare this month to the same month last year (year over year) instead of the previous month?
It removes seasonal effects that distort month to month comparisons
It always produces higher growth numbers, which look better in the monthly report
It requires less historical data to calculate correctly
It removes the need to check the data for any outliers
Year over year comparisons hold the season constant, so differences reflect real change.
What is a cohort in cohort analysis?
Users who share a starting trait, such as sign-up month
All users who visited the site at any time today
A random sample of users chosen for one arm of an A/B test
The top 10% of customers ranked by total revenue
Cohorts are defined by a shared event in a time window, so their behavior can be tracked over time.
In a retention cohort table, the January cohort shows 40% active in month 1, while the March cohort shows 55% in month 1. What does this suggest?
Something changed by March that improved early retention
March users signed up for longer contracts by default
The January cohort is too small to analyze
Retention tables cannot be compared between cohorts
Comparing the same age across cohorts isolates changes in product or acquisition that affect retention.
Why can overall average retention look stable while each cohort's retention is falling?
A growing share of newer users can hide declines in each cohort
Averages always hide every trend in the data completely
Each cohort is calculated with a different retention formula
Retention can only be computed once per year for any product
Aggregates mix users of different ages. Cohort analysis separates them to show real behavior.
In hypothesis testing, what does a p-value of 0.03 mean?
If the null were true, results this extreme would occur about 3% of the time
There is a 3% chance that the null hypothesis is actually true for this data
There is a 97% chance that the alternative hypothesis is true
The measured effect size between the groups is exactly 3%
The p-value is computed assuming the null is true. It is not the probability that the null is true.
An A/B test compares conversion rates of two page versions. What is the null hypothesis?
There is no difference in conversion rate between the versions
Version B converts better than version A for most users in the test
Version A converts better than version B for most users
Both versions convert visitors at a rate of exactly 0%
The null hypothesis states no effect; the test asks whether the data give enough evidence to reject it.
A team checks 20 different metrics in one experiment at alpha = 0.05 and celebrates one significant result. What is the problem?
With many tests, about one false positive is expected by chance
Alpha should be raised to 0.5 when an experiment tracks many metrics
Significant results cannot happen with 20 metrics
The sample size is irrelevant to significance
This is the multiple comparisons problem. Pre-registering a primary metric or correcting (for example Bonferroni) addresses it.
data-visualization: You need to show monthly revenue over three years. Which chart type fits best?
Line chart
Pie chart
Scatter plot
Treemap
Line charts show change over continuous time clearly; pie charts show parts of a whole at one moment.
You need to compare sales across 12 product categories. Which chart is usually clearest?
Sorted horizontal bar chart
Pie chart with 12 slices
Line chart connecting categories
3D cone chart
People compare lengths more accurately than angles, and sorting plus horizontal labels makes 12 categories easy to read.
Which chart best shows the relationship between two numeric variables, such as ad spend and sales?
Scatter plot
Stacked bar chart
Donut chart
Area chart
Scatter plots show each observation by two coordinates, revealing correlation, clusters and outliers.
Why are pie charts generally discouraged for comparing many similar values?
People judge angles and areas less accurately than lengths
Pie charts cannot display percentages or labels at all
Pie charts are not supported by most charting tools
Pie charts only work when the data has negative values
Perception research (Cleveland and McGill) ranks position and length above angle and area for accuracy.
In narrative visualization, what is the purpose of an annotation such as "Price cut launched here" on a line chart?
Directing attention to the event that explains the change
Making the chart look busier and more detailed overall
Replacing the axis labels with a shorter description
Hiding data points that do not fit the intended story
Annotations connect data to context, telling the audience what to notice and why.
Which chart title best supports a narrative visualization?
Support tickets fell 30% after the new help center launched
Chart 3: support ticket data for the last twelve months
Support tickets by month, January to December
Monthly data exported from the ticketing system
An action title states the takeaway, so the audience understands the message before studying the details.
In a chart about one important product among ten, what is an effective way to highlight it?
Color the focus product strongly and show the others in muted gray
Give each of the ten products its own different bright, saturated color
Make all lines dashed except one dotted line
Remove the other products from the axis labels only
Using gray for context and one accent color makes the focus stand out immediately.
Which color scheme fits a map of unemployment rate from low to high?
Sequential scheme, light to dark of one hue
Qualitative scheme with several unrelated hues
Rainbow scheme with many hues
Random colors per region
Ordered numeric data needs a sequential scheme where lightness clearly encodes order.
Which color scheme fits data with a meaningful midpoint, such as temperature change above and below zero?
Diverging scheme with a neutral middle
Sequential scheme using one hue
Qualitative scheme of unrelated hues
Grayscale scheme with no hue at all
Diverging schemes use two hues that move away from a neutral center to show direction and magnitude.
Why is a red-green only color encoding risky?
Red-green deficiency is the most common type of color blindness
Red and green inks cannot be printed next to each other on the same page
Most web browsers do not render pure green correctly
Red and green use more printer ink than other colors
Pair colors with lightness differences, labels or patterns, or use colorblind-safe palettes.
What is the most common recommended layout principle for a dashboard?
Put the most important KPIs at the top left, details below
Put the most important KPIs at the bottom right, details above
Spread the charts randomly to keep the layout interesting
Put every metric into one large table with no charts at all
In left-to-right reading cultures, viewers scan from the top left first, so key information goes there.
A dashboard has 25 charts on one screen. What is the best improvement?
Keep the few decision-driving metrics and move the rest to drill-downs
Shrink every chart even further so that more of them fit on screen
Add entrance animations to each chart to keep viewers engaged
Use a different chart type for each metric to add visual variety
Effective dashboards answer specific questions at a glance; overload hides what matters.
Why should KPI tiles on a dashboard usually show a comparison, such as vs last month or vs target?
A number alone does not show whether it is good or bad
Comparisons make the KPI tiles load faster in the browser
Dashboard standards require exactly two numbers per tile
Showing a comparison removes the need for any chart titles
Context like a target or previous period turns a number into information a viewer can act on.
What does Edward Tufte's data-ink ratio encourage?
Spending most of the ink on data and removing decoration
Using as much ink as possible to make every chart bold
Printing all charts using black ink only for clarity
Adding a background image to every chart for context
Tufte argues that heavy gridlines, borders, 3D effects and decoration should be reduced so the data stands out.
Which change increases the data-ink ratio of a bar chart?
Removing heavy gridlines and the 3D effect
Adding a soft drop shadow to each of the bars
Adding a patterned background
Adding a thick border around the chart
Gridlines, shadows and 3D are non-data ink. Removing them focuses attention on the bars.
What is "chartjunk" in Tufte's terminology?
Decoration that adds no information, such as fake 3D effects
Charts that were made with free or open source charting software
Charts that use more than two colors for their series
Charts that contain too few data points to be useful
Chartjunk is decoration that adds no information and can distort reading.
Why should the value axis of a bar chart start at zero?
Bar length encodes value, so a cut axis exaggerates gaps
Most charting software tools require it for bar charts
Starting at zero makes the bars thinner and easier to read
It automatically hides any negative values in the data
With a truncated axis, a 2% difference can look like a doubling. Line charts can sometimes use non-zero baselines.
A chart has two y-axes with different scales for two lines. What is the main risk?
Scale choices can create a fake correlation or crossing point
The chart can no longer show more than two lines in total
Dual axes always double the file size of the exported chart
The x-axis must then be switched to a logarithmic scale
The apparent relationship depends on arbitrary scaling of each axis, which can mislead readers.
When is a logarithmic y-axis appropriate?
When data spans several orders of magnitude
When all values fall between 0 and 10
When you want small differences to look bigger
When the data contains many negative values
Log scales show equal percentage changes as equal distances. They cannot show zero or negatives and need clear labeling.
A bubble chart sizes bubbles by radius proportional to value. What is the problem?
Area grows with the square of radius, so big values look exaggerated
Bubbles in a bubble chart are not allowed to overlap each other in any layout
Radius is a property that cannot encode numeric values at all
Bubble charts must use only one color for every bubble shown
Viewers perceive area, so bubble area, not radius, should be proportional to the value.
excel: In Excel, what does the last argument FALSE mean in =VLOOKUP(A2, D:F, 3, FALSE)?
Find an exact match for A2
Return the value from column D
Search from the bottom up
Ignore case when matching text
FALSE (or 0) requests an exact match. TRUE or omitting it uses approximate match, which needs sorted data.
Why can VLOOKUP not directly return a value from a column to the LEFT of the lookup column?
It searches the first column of the range and returns from columns to its right
It only works with numeric data, so text columns to the left of it are always skipped
It requires the whole table to be sorted in descending order first
It cannot look up values stored on a different worksheet
The lookup column must be the leftmost in table_array. INDEX/MATCH or XLOOKUP remove this limitation.
A VLOOKUP returns #N/A for "ABC123" even though it appears in the table. What is a common cause?
Extra spaces or a text vs number mismatch in the values
The workbook is saved in the .xlsx file format
The column index number in the formula points to an empty column
The worksheet is protected with a password
Hidden trailing spaces or numbers stored as text prevent an exact match. TRIM or VALUE can fix the data.
What does =XLOOKUP("P7", A2:A100, C2:C100, "Not found") return if "P7" is not in A2:A100?
The text Not found
#N/A
The last value in C2:C100
XLOOKUP's fourth argument, if_not_found, replaces the #N/A error with a custom value.
Which is an advantage of XLOOKUP over VLOOKUP in Excel 365?
It can return values to the left and defaults to an exact match
It works in every older Excel version, including Excel 2010
It is the only lookup function that supports wildcard matching
It automatically sorts the lookup range before searching it
XLOOKUP uses separate lookup and return arrays and exact match by default. It is not available in Excel 2016 or earlier.
What does =MATCH("Kiwi", {"Apple","Kiwi","Pear"}, 0) return?
"Kiwi"
TRUE
MATCH returns the relative position of the item; with match_type 0 it finds the exact match at position 2.
What does =INDEX(B2:B10, MATCH("Bob", A2:A10, 0)) do?
Returns the column B value on the row where column A equals Bob
Counts how many times the name Bob appears in column A
Returns the row number where the name Bob appears in column B
Sorts the values in column B by the names in column A
MATCH finds Bob's position in A2:A10, and INDEX returns the item at that position in B2:B10.
Why is INDEX-MATCH often more robust than VLOOKUP with a hard-coded column number?
Inserting a column in the table does not shift its return column
It works only on data that is sorted in ascending order
It ignores blank cells in the lookup range automatically, unlike VLOOKUP
It converts numbers stored as text into real numbers
VLOOKUP's column index is a fixed number that becomes wrong when columns are inserted; INDEX references the actual column.
What is a PivotTable mainly used for?
Summarizing and grouping large data by category without formulas
Encrypting a workbook so it can only be opened with a password
Drawing free-form shapes and diagrams on top of a worksheet
Recording macros in VBA to automate repetitive tasks
PivotTables aggregate (sum, count, average) data by fields placed in Rows, Columns, Values and Filters.
You add new rows below the source data of a PivotTable, but the pivot does not show them after Refresh. What is the best fix?
Convert the source data into an Excel Table so the range grows
Delete the workbook and recreate the PivotTable from scratch
Turn off automatic calculation for the whole workbook
Move the PivotTable to a new worksheet and refresh it again
A PivotTable based on a fixed range ignores rows outside it. A Table (Ctrl + T) expands automatically.
In a PivotTable, a Revenue field placed in Values shows "Count of Revenue" instead of a sum. What is the likely reason?
The column contains text or blank cells, so Excel uses Count
The PivotTable is linked to a source table stored in another workbook
The Revenue field is also placed in the Filters area
The workbook is set to use manual calculation mode
Excel defaults to Sum only when the column is fully numeric. Text values (such as numbers stored as text) or blanks make it default to Count.
Which conditional formatting rule highlights entire rows where column C equals "Late" when applied to A2:F100?
Use a formula: =$C2="Late"
Use a formula: =C$2="Late"
Use a formula: =$C$2="Late"
Use a formula: =C2:C100="Late"
Locking the column ($C) while leaving the row relative (2) lets each row check its own C value.
What does the conditional formatting option "Color Scales" do?
Shades cells with a gradient based on their relative values
Changes the theme colors used across every sheet in the whole workbook
Applies the same fill color to every non-empty cell
Colors each cell based on who last edited its contents
Color scales map low to high values onto a color gradient, giving a quick heatmap view.
What does =IF(B2>=90, "A", IF(B2>=80, "B", "C")) return when B2 is 85?
B
A
C
FALSE
85 is not >= 90, so the second IF runs; 85 >= 80 is true, so it returns B.
In Excel 2019 and later, which function can replace deeply nested IF formulas by testing conditions in order?
IFS
SUMIFS
IFERROR
COUNTIF
IFS(condition1, value1, condition2, value2, ...) returns the value for the first true condition, avoiding nested IFs.
What does =IF(AND(A2>0, B2>0), "OK", "Check") return when A2 is 5 and B2 is 0?
Check
OK
TRUE
#VALUE!
AND requires all conditions to be true; B2>0 is false, so the IF returns the value_if_false argument.
How can you restrict a cell to a dropdown of allowed values such as "Open", "Closed", "Pending"?
Data Validation with Allow set to List
Conditional formatting with a color scale
Protect Sheet with a password
A PivotTable filter
Data > Data Validation > List creates an in-cell dropdown and rejects other entries by default.
Which Data Validation setting prevents users from entering a date earlier than today?
Allow Date, greater than or equal to =TODAY()
Allow Whole number, between 1 and 31
Allow Text length, equal to 10 characters
Allow List, with the source set to =TODAY()
Date validation with a formula like =TODAY() as the minimum blocks earlier dates.
What is Power Query in Excel mainly used for?
Importing, cleaning and reshaping data with repeatable steps
Writing VBA macros that run when users click buttons
Designing printable page layouts with headers and footers
Creating interactive 3D maps of geographic data
Power Query (Get & Transform) records transformation steps that can be refreshed when the source changes.
Your monthly sales are in columns Jan, Feb, Mar and so on. Which Power Query operation turns them into two columns, Month and Sales?
Unpivot Columns
Pivot Column
Merge Queries
Group By
Unpivot turns wide columns into attribute-value rows, the tidy format needed for PivotTables and charts.
tableau: In Tableau, what does the calculated field SUM([Profit]) / SUM([Sales]) compute in a view by Region?
The profit ratio for each region
The profit of each order, then summed
The total sales for all regions
The average of row-level profit ratios
Aggregating before dividing gives a ratio of totals at the view's level of detail. Dividing row by row and averaging gives a different result.
Why does Tableau show an error for the calculation [Sales] / SUM([Sales])?
It mixes an aggregate and a non-aggregate argument
Division is not supported between fields in calculated fields
Field names cannot be repeated
SUM only works on dimensions
Tableau requires arguments to be all aggregated or all row level; wrap [Sales] in an aggregation or use a table calculation.
Which is valid Tableau calculated field syntax for labeling sales above 1000 as High and the rest as Low?
IF [Sales] > 1000 THEN "High" ELSE "Low" END
CASE [Sales] WHEN > 1000 THEN "High" ELSE "Low" END
IIF([Sales] > 1000) THEN "High"
WHEN [Sales] > 1000 RETURN "High"
Tableau IF statements use IF ... THEN ... ELSE ... END syntax; CASE compares exact values, not ranges.
What is a Tableau parameter?
A user-controlled value that can drive calculations, filters or reference lines
A field from the data source that users are not allowed to edit or rename in the workbook
A saved copy of the data extract stored inside the workbook
A Tableau Server setting that controls who can view a workbook
Parameters are global values controlled by the user, often via a parameter control, and must be referenced in calculations or filters to have an effect.
You create a parameter "Top N" but changing it does nothing in the view. What is the most likely reason?
No calculation, filter or set references the parameter yet
Parameters only work with extracts, not with live connections
The parameter must be a string type for changes to apply
Parameter changes only apply after the workbook is republished
A parameter alone has no effect; it must be used in, for example, a Top N filter or a calculated field.
How can a user switch a chart between showing Sales and Profit with one control?
A parameter listing both options plus a calculated field returning the chosen one
Create two separate data sources, one per measure, and blend them on the Region field
Add a context filter on Sales and a second one on Profit
Apply a FIXED LOD expression to Profit and hide the Sales axis
A parameter plus a CASE or IF calculated field is the standard measure-swap pattern.
What does {FIXED [Customer ID] : MIN([Order Date])} return?
Each customer's first order date, regardless of the view
The single earliest order date in the entire data source
The order date of the first row currently shown in the view
The total number of orders placed by each customer
A FIXED LOD computes at the specified dimension, here each customer, independently of what is in the view.
How do INCLUDE and EXCLUDE LOD expressions differ from FIXED?
They compute relative to the view, adding or removing dimensions
They ignore all filters in the workbook, including context filters
They work only on extracts and fail on live connections
They always return strings instead of numbers or dates
FIXED uses only the listed dimensions; INCLUDE adds dimensions to the view's level, and EXCLUDE removes them.
A dimension filter does not affect a FIXED LOD calculation. Which change makes the filter apply to it?
Add the dimension filter to context
Convert the filter to a measure filter
Move the LOD to the Rows shelf
Change FIXED to MIN
In Tableau's order of operations, FIXED LODs are computed before regular dimension filters but after context filters.
In Tableau, what is a Story?
A sequence of sheets or dashboards that walks viewers through findings
A data source that has a written text description attached to explain each of its fields
A calculated field that returns full sentences instead of numbers
A Tableau Server schedule that refreshes extracts every night
Stories present a narrative with captions, each story point showing a view or dashboard in a chosen state.
Which dashboard action lets clicking a bar in one sheet filter the other sheets on the dashboard?
Filter action
URL action
Go to Sheet action
Highlight action
A filter action passes the selected values as filters to target sheets on the dashboard.
Why might a dashboard designer prefer a Fixed dashboard size over Automatic?
It gives a predictable layout and can improve server caching
Fixed size allows unlimited sheets
Automatic sizing is not supported once a dashboard is published to Tableau Server
Fixed size removes the need for filters
Fixed sizes render consistently on all screens; Automatic resizes and can shift elements unpredictably.
In classic Tableau data blending, what defines the primary data source?
The data source of the first field placed in the view
The data source with the most rows
The data source that was connected most recently
The data source that has the larger number of columns
The first source used becomes primary (blue check); secondary sources (orange check) are aggregated and joined on linking fields.
How does data blending differ from a join in Tableau?
Blending aggregates each source first, then combines; a join combines rows first
Blending can only combine sources that live in the same database, while joins work across any
Joins are only available on Tableau Server, not in Tableau Desktop
Blending duplicates every row of the secondary data source
Blending works like a post-aggregation left join on linking fields, which avoids row duplication across different granularities.
In Tableau, what is the main difference between a set and a group?
A set splits members into In and Out, possibly dynamically; a group merges members
A set can only contain measures, while a group can only contain dates
Sets are limited to 10 members each, while groups can contain any number of members
Sets only work on Tableau Server, while groups work everywhere
Sets split data into In and Out and can update by condition or top N; groups merge dimension members into higher-level labels.
Which filter is applied first in Tableau's order of operations among these?
Extract filter
Dimension filter
Measure filter
Table calculation filter
The order is extract, data source, context, then FIXED LOD, dimension, INCLUDE/EXCLUDE LOD, measure, and finally table calculation filters.
You want a Top 10 customers filter to apply only within the selected Region. What should you do?
Add the Region filter to context
Turn Region into a measure
Use a table calculation filter on Region
Put Region on the Detail mark
Top N filters are evaluated before regular dimension filters. Making Region a context filter evaluates it first.
What does LAST() = 0 used as a filter typically achieve in a view?
Shows only the last mark per partition while keeping table calculations intact
Removes all null values from the view before any of the table calculations can run
Shows only the earliest date that exists in the whole data source
Filters out the most recent row from the extract during refresh
Table calculation filters hide marks after calculations run, so running totals stay correct.
How do you show values as currency with no decimals on a Tableau axis?
Set the field's number format to Currency (Custom) with 0 decimals
Wrap the field in STR() inside a new calculated field
Change the field's data type to string in the data source, then add a $ prefix
Use a parameter to round each value before it is drawn
Number formatting changes display without altering the data type. Converting to string breaks aggregation and axes.
Which formatting choice best follows good visual practice in a Tableau bar chart?
Light or no gridlines, direct labels, and color only when it encodes data
Heavy gridlines, a dark border and a gradient fill on every bar to add depth
A different bright color for every bar, applied by default
Bold fonts for every label, title and tooltip in the chart
Minimal formatting puts focus on the data. Use color only when it carries meaning.
power-bi: In Power BI, what is the key difference between a calculated column and a measure?
Columns are computed per row at refresh; measures at query time in filter context
Measures are stored per row in the table; calculated columns are computed on the fly
Calculated columns are written in M; measures are written in SQL
They are identical features that only differ in their display name
Calculated columns consume memory and use row context; measures aggregate dynamically based on filters in visuals.
What does the DAX measure Total Sales = SUMX(Sales, Sales[Qty] * Sales[Price]) do?
Multiplies Qty by Price for each row, then sums the results
Sums Qty and Price separately, then multiplies the totals
Returns the maximum Qty times the maximum Price
Counts rows where Qty and Price are both non-blank
SUMX is an iterator: it evaluates the expression row by row and sums it, which is correct for line totals.
What does CALCULATE([Total Sales], Product[Color] = "Red") return?
Total Sales with filter context changed to red products only
The number of distinct products in the model whose color is red
Total Sales for all product colors except red
A table containing only the red products
CALCULATE evaluates an expression under modified filter context; it is the most important function in DAX.
What does ALL(Product) do when used inside CALCULATE?
Removes filters from the Product table for that calculation
Selects all columns of Product for display
Counts all rows in Product
Adds a filter that keeps every product visible in visuals
ALL removes filters, which is commonly used to compute a grand total for percent-of-total measures.
Which DAX function divides two values and returns BLANK (or an alternate result) instead of an error when the denominator is zero?
DIVIDE
QUOTIENT
MOD
IFERROR
DIVIDE(numerator, denominator, alternateResult) safely handles division by zero.
Which DAX time intelligence function compares to the same period last year?
SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR
STARTOFQUARTER
EOMONTH
PREVIOUSDAY
CALCULATE([Sales], SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR('Date'[Date])) returns last year's value for the current period; it needs a proper date table.
In Power Query, what language is used for transformation steps?
M
DAX
Python
T-SQL
Power Query steps are written in M. DAX is used for measures and calculated columns in the model.
A Power Query step references column "Amount" but the source renames it to "Total". What happens on refresh?
The refresh fails with a column not found error
Power Query automatically maps Total to Amount
The Amount column is silently filled with zeros
Power BI skips the broken step and continues
Steps reference columns by name, so renamed source columns break steps like Changed Type.
What does query folding mean in Power Query?
Steps are translated into a native query run by the source
Queries are compressed into a smaller file before refresh
Several queries are merged into one table automatically
Steps are hidden from the Applied Steps pane to save space
When folding works, filtering and grouping happen in the database, which improves refresh performance.
Which Power Query operation combines two tables with the same columns by stacking rows?
Append Queries
Merge Queries
Pivot Column
Group By
Append stacks rows (like SQL UNION ALL); Merge joins tables on matching columns.
What is a star schema in Power BI data modeling?
Fact tables in the center related to surrounding dimension tables
A single flat table that holds every column of the model
Tables connected one after another in a long chain of relationships
Several fact tables joined directly to each other by keys
Microsoft recommends star schemas: facts hold events and numbers, dimensions describe them, which makes DAX simpler and faster.
In a relationship between a Customers dimension and a Sales fact table, what is the usual cardinality?
One-to-many from Customers to Sales
Many-to-many
One-to-one
Many-to-one from Customers to Sales
Each customer appears once in Customers and many times in Sales.
What is the default and generally recommended cross-filter direction for a one-to-many relationship?
Single, from the one side to the many side
Both directions
None
From the many side to the one side only
Single direction avoids ambiguity and performance issues; bidirectional filtering should be used sparingly.
Why should you mark a dedicated table as a Date table in Power BI?
So time intelligence functions work with a continuous date range
So the date table refreshes faster than the other tables
Because visuals cannot display dates unless a table is marked
To hide the date table from report users in the Fields pane
Marking a date table with one row per day and no gaps tells Power BI to use it for DAX time intelligence, which then works reliably.
Which report design choice usually improves a Power BI report page?
A few key visuals in a clear grid with consistent colors
As many visuals as will fit on the page at once
A different color theme on each page of the report to separate topics
A gauge visual for every single metric in the model
Focused pages with consistent formatting are easier to read and perform better.
Which Power BI feature lets a report user right-click a data point and go to a detail page filtered to that item?
Drillthrough
Bookmarks
Sync slicers
Field parameters
Drillthrough pages accept a field and open filtered to the selected value from another page.
How is row-level security (RLS) defined in Power BI Desktop?
By creating roles with DAX filter expressions
By hiding sensitive columns in the Fields pane
By password-protecting the .pbix file itself
By deleting restricted rows in Power Query
RLS roles use DAX filters, such as [Region] = "North", and users are assigned to roles in the Power BI service.
A dynamic RLS rule should show each salesperson only their own rows. Which DAX function is typically used?
USERPRINCIPALNAME()
TODAY()
SELECTEDVALUE()
RELATED()
USERPRINCIPALNAME returns the signed-in user's UPN (often their email), which is compared to a column in the security table.
A Power BI semantic model uses Import mode with on-premises SQL Server. What is required for scheduled refresh in the Power BI service?
An on-premises data gateway
A Premium capacity license in all cases
A DirectQuery connection
Publishing to the web
The service is in the cloud, so it needs a gateway to reach on-premises sources during refresh.
How does DirectQuery mode differ from Import mode for data freshness?
DirectQuery queries the source at view time instead of importing data
DirectQuery stores a full compressed copy of the data inside Power BI
DirectQuery data refreshes only once a week on a fixed schedule
Import mode always shows real-time data without any refresh
Import caches data and needs refresh; DirectQuery queries the source live, trading speed for freshness.
